newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil strike spreads to two more coffee ports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil strike spreads to two more coffee ports.

text.p: A strike by Brazilian stevedores in the key port of Santos spread to two other coffee ports on Friday as workers protested about the progress of the government's port privatisation programme, officials said.

Port officials in Vitoria and Rio de Janeiro, the country's two most important exit points for coffee after Santos, confirmed early Friday loading operations had stopped in support of a 24-hour strike called by the National Stevedores Federation.
But in the north/northeast of the country, officials at Recife, the region's key sugar port, said operations were continuing normally and added they did not know of any strike plans.
Officials at Maceio, the other sugar port in the region, could not immediately be reached for comment.

In Paranagua, the country's key soybean and soy products port, the stevedores union decided last night to halt work for one hour at 1300 local (1600 GMT) but that work at the grains export terminal would continue uninterrupted.
A union official confirmed at 0715 local time this morning that the port was operating normally at that time.

Stevedores in Santos have virtually halted all loading and unloading operations since Wednesday morning over a ruling which allows a steel company to use its own workers as stevedores in its private terminal at the port.

Antonio Pinheiro, first treasurer at the Santos stevedores union, said unions across the country were faxing through strike reports and that information on the extent of the stoppage would be available later today.
Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
